To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
extreme winter events can have a large impact on the carbon uptake of sub-Arctic peatlands.

(1) An extreme winter event in northern Norway in 2013-2014 caused severe damage to the dwarf shrub Calluna vulgaris, (2) This reduced the carbon uptake by 12% in the summer of that year, (3) The dwarf shrub Empetrum nigerum was resilient to the extreme cold and was not affected, (4) The warm and sunny summer stimulated photosynthesis, but also increased ecosystem respiation, limiting net carbon uptake, and

an extreme winter event that damaged the shrubs Calluna vulgaris (heather) and Empetrum (crowberry) reduced gross primary productivity (GPP) by 14 g C m- 2 in 2014, but that the ecosystem eventually recovered to the same level of GPP as in 2015 and previous years.
